problem:
The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2},$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the particle's acceleration at $t=1$ second.

$a(1)=$
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}) \\  & =15{t}^{2}-4t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(15{t}^{2}-4t) \\  & =30t-4\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=1$ second, we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =30(1)-4 \\  & =26\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
